comparator.name: Dentistry (Tandheelkunde)
comparator.institution: Academic Centre for Dentistry Amsterdam (ACTA), VU Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: The current ACTA curriculum comprises 60 compulsory EC in each of three years. It combines oral biology, cariology, periodontal disease, restorative and preventive dentistry, progressive clinical skills and a 14 EC supervised research placement with a thesis and oral defence.
components: Lijn professionele ontwikkeling en academische vorming 1
Lijn professionele ontwikkeling en academische vorming 2

exception.reason: UCR offers biomedical science, public health, laboratory methods and health psychology. The courses do not provide the sustained study of oral disease, dental restoration and supervised patient treatment that defines ACTA’s Dentistry degree.
exception.curriculumContext: The current ACTA curriculum comprises 60 compulsory EC in each of three years. It combines oral biology, cariology, periodontal disease, restorative and preventive dentistry, progressive clinical skills and a 14 EC supervised research placement with a thesis and oral defence.

registryRow.evidence: The bachelor directly invites students who want to help people improve their health through dentistry.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Oral health improvement is central; general biomedical/public-health study contributes background, not oral care practice.

registryRow.student_interest: looking beyond teeth to the whole patient
registryRow.evidence: ACTA stresses that dentists should understand each patient as a unique person rather than only treating teeth.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam || Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Whole-patient approach explicitly supported; psychology is relevant but does not replace integrated dental-medical assessment.

registryRow.evidence: The programme presents dentistry as the integration of patient care, scientific knowledge and technical skill.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam || Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Science, technique and communication are integrated in dentistry; generic data/biomedicine alone does not implement dental technology.

registryRow.evidence: Students learn to assess oral health scientifically before choosing a treatment.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Oral diagnosis supported by current competencies; psychodiagnostics is a different clinical field.

registryRow.evidence: The programme explicitly teaches students to involve patients in developing treatment plans.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Shared treatment planning is explicit; rhetoric is not dental care-plan design.

registryRow.evidence: Prevention is central to the programme’s model of dentistry.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Prevention explicit; epidemiology is relevant population background, not caries/periodontal clinical prevention.

registryRow.evidence: ACTA describes the dentist as a scientifically informed problem-solver.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Clinical problem solving explicit; generic disease reasoning lacks dental diagnostic/treatment progression.

registryRow.evidence: Students learn to collect, assess and apply scientific information in oral care.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Critical scientific dental practice and research explicitly supported; statistics contributes methods without dental capstone.

registryRow.evidence: The curriculum explicitly integrates clinical skill development with theory and science.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Dental skills explicit in curriculum; no UCR specialist clinical content.

registryRow.evidence: The programme identifies spatial insight, dexterity and precision as qualities developed for dental practice.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Manual precision/spatial skills explicit; general laboratory work is not tooth restoration or dental instrumentation.

registryRow.evidence: Communication is a central professional competence throughout the bachelor.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam || Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Confident patient communication explicit; rhetoric supplies general skills, no patient-care practicum.

registryRow.evidence: Students learn to treat patients with empathy, respect and professional expertise.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Empathy/respect explicit; psychology is useful background without integrated oral care.

registryRow.evidence: The programme frames dentistry as guiding people in their health and wellbeing, not only performing procedures.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Health/wellbeing guidance supported; biopsychosocial psychology offers partial background, not oral prevention delivery.

registryRow.student_interest: care for patients of different ages and backgrounds
registryRow.evidence: ACTA explicitly teaches care across ages, backgrounds, identities and care needs.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: All ages/backgrounds supported; developmental psychology contributes background without oral-care provision.

registryRow.evidence: Creating a safe and accessible treatment environment is presented as a core responsibility.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Accessible inclusive treatment explicitly supported; broad social justice courses do not establish oral service/care expertise.

registryRow.student_interest: how socioeconomic conditions affect oral health
registryRow.evidence: Students are asked to consider patients’ socioeconomic circumstances as part of responsible care.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Socioeconomic patient context explicit; general sociology/economics does not form dental public health progression.

registryRow.evidence: The programme connects social responsibility in dentistry to diversity among patients.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Diversity explicitly supported; leadership diversity is workplace-general, not specialist dental curriculum.

registryRow.evidence: Collaboration in multidisciplinary teams is named as a core professional competence.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Multidisciplinary teamwork explicit; generic collaboration not clinical team competence.

registryRow.evidence: Research groups offer bachelor research placements and the programme trains critical scientific thinking.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Current14EC research placement/thesis and methods verified; not old16EC placement.

registryRow.evidence: The prospective-student material presents virtual drilling equipment and preclinical practice as concrete learning experiences.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Virtual drilling is current promotional illustration, not an independent route or guaranteed named course.

registryRow.evidence: The current curriculum prepares third-year students to begin treating patients with uncomplicated plaque-related disease.
registryRow.source_title: Nieuw curriculum Tandheelkunde - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Current official new-curriculum page explicitly states Year3 treatment of simple plaque-related disease; current OER patientcare corroborates. No UCR equivalent.

registryRow.student_interest: preventive care for vulnerable older people
registryRow.evidence: Home visits for vulnerable elderly patients are now a recurring part of the ACTA dental curriculum.
registryRow.source_title: Students to visit elderly with oral care bike - Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: 2025official news describes elderly preventive-care bike project; real programme activity, not a fixed degree route or guaranteed cohort placement.

registryRow.evidence: ACTA presents responsibility for underserved and vulnerable groups as part of the dentist’s role.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Inhoud - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam || Students to visit elderly with oral care bike - Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Social responsibility explicit; current official community-care example corroborates, no independent dental-health-equity UCR alternative.

registryRow.evidence: The bachelor is the first half of the six-year route to qualification as a dentist.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Toekomst - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Dentist career requires subsequent master; not a bachelor qualification or construction generator.

registryRow.evidence: Solo practices, group practices and employed practice roles are named graduate outcomes.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Toekomst - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Dental practice is post-master outcome; not bachelor elective content or UCR equivalence.

registryRow.evidence: ACTA presents teaching and research roles as later career possibilities.
registryRow.source_title: Bachelor Tandheelkunde - Toekomst - Academisch Centrum Tandheelkunde Amsterdam

interestConstructionAssessment.finding: Education/research careers after master explicitly listed; not evidence for independent bachelor specialization.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: UCR courses cover cells, tissues, organs, microbiology, immunity, pharmacology, health behaviour and research methods. Anatomy and biomedical laboratory work provide related foundations. They do not build into oral diagnosis, restoration, endodontics, periodontal treatment, dental radiology or patient care.

candidateAssessment.label: Biomedical Science and Patient-Centred Health
candidateAssessment.reason: A feasible plan develops biomedical knowledge, laboratory techniques, research design and communication. Functional Anatomy and Life Science Laboratory supply anatomical and experimental work, but do not teach dental anatomy in clinical practice, restoration or treatment.

candidateAssessment.label: Health Equity, Prevention and Access to Care
candidateAssessment.reason: A feasible plan combines epidemiology, health behaviour, inequality and public policy. It develops a population-health perspective without the dental prevention, diagnosis and treatment that define the target.

audience.programmeDescription: ACTA’s Dutch-taught Dentistry degree combines oral biology, disease, prevention and restoration with clinical training and research. Students progress from preclinical practice to supervised patient treatment and care planning.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in biomedical science, laboratory methods, public health and health psychology. It does not provide ACTA’s progression through oral diagnosis, restoration, periodontal care and supervised dental treatment.

curriculum.limitation: All 180 EC are compulsory. The curriculum includes practical and clinical attendance requirements and a 14 EC supervised research placement.

componentNotes.y1-t-b1intro: The Dutch language assessment or required follow-up course is part of this unit.
componentNotes.y2-t-b2ltv2a: Entry depends on earlier oral biology, restoration and dental skills work.
componentNotes.y3-t-b3wstage: Requires passing first-year research methods and second-year research preparation. Includes a thesis and oral defence.
